subject: Linguistics
title: Japanese Writing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Japanese Writing usable.

hook.text: Japanese uses three scripts at once: kanji, hiragana, and katakana—often in the same sentence.

buildup.text: Kanji (Chinese characters) represent content words; hiragana marks grammar; katakana writes foreign words.

discovery.text: This triple system evolved because Japanese needed to adapt Chinese writing to a very different grammar.

twist.text: A single sentence might use all three scripts plus romaji (Latin letters)—and it's perfectly normal.

climax.text: Japanese literacy requires knowing about 2,100 kanji plus two complete syllabaries.

punchline.text: Three scripts in one sentence—only Japanese.

quiz.question: What is katakana primarily used for in Japanese?
